text:
Lina: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today’s runtime segment. I promised a live thread for outstanding roadmap questions on microbatching, per-tenant batching policies, and kernel prewarm. Drop questions here and we'll triage.
Tom: Quick one — can you clarify the rollout timeline for per-tenant batching controls? We need finer knobs for a big customer next month.
Samir: +1 on timeline. Also: will that be a Console UI toggle or infra config only?
Lina: Plan is phased: API/infra v1 (config flags + annotations) in 3 weeks, console exposure as a beta the quarter after. Infra-first so platform teams can test.
Anya: For infra v1 — do we expect any perf regression while we add per-tenant queues? Concerned about tail latency.
Jordan: We ran a small experiment — added tenant labeling and a per-tenant micro-queue. Median stable, p99 increased ~5-7ms on p4x runs. We think KV cache isolation and routing improvements will remove that.
Priya: Can you share the routing change outline? We need to know compatibility with sidecar routing.
Lina: Short version: routing will support policy tags (latency-tier, cost-tier, tenant). Default policy maintains current greedy packing; new policies opt into tenant isolation or isolated pools. Sidecar routing will respect policy headers.
Tom: Is there a recommended policy for latency-sensitive tenants? e.g., minimum batch size or batching disabled?
Samir: We should avoid disabling batching entirely. For latency-sensitive, use small max_batch and aggressive prewarm + dedicated pool.
Anya: About prewarm — any update on kernel prewarm hooks for long-context models? We saw large cold-starts when context changes.
Jordan: Kernel team prototype: a background prewarm thread that warms kv-cache and attention kernels for hot sequences. Works well for recurring prefixes, reduces first token latency by ~50-70ms in tests.
Priya: Is that prewarm compatible with quantized kernels (4-bit) and CPU fallback?
Jordan: Yes, prototype supports q4 and fp16. CPU fallback will pre-compile slower codepaths but still helps; we need more telemetry for edge cases.
Lina: Action: kernel team will add prewarm telemetry flags to the canary next week. We'll surface a per-model metric in Console.
DevBot: Canary deployment started for kernel-prewarm-feature at 1769991400. 6/8 instances healthy.
Tom: Related ask — can we get a short recipe for customers: "latency-sensitive profile" to paste into infra? e.g., configs for pool, batch, cache.
Samir: Draft snippet:

```
policy: latency-sensitive
min_batch: 1
max_batch: 8
prewarm: true
dedicated_pool: true
kv_cache: enabled
cache_ttl_ms: 60000
```

Use as starting point.
Anya: For cache TTL — any guidance on eviction vs memory pressure tradeoffs? We had a case where high cache TTL caused OOMs.
Jordan: We'll add an autoscaling hook that reduces cache TTL under memory pressure; default will be 60s but recommend monitoring resident memory.
Priya: How about observability — will we report per-tenant token cost breakdown? That’s critical for chargebacks.
Lina: Yes, cost + latency per route and per-tenant will be in the Optimize tab beta. Timeline: sampling in 2 weeks, full metrics in ~6 weeks.
Tom: Are there any breaking changes to the RPC surface for clients? SDK changes?
Samir: No breaking RPCs. New flags via headers and the SDK will add convenience helpers in the next minor release.
Anya: Testing note: can we get a private canary pool to validate tenant policies before wider rollout? Some customers want to try.
Lina: Good point — Dedicated teams will expose a private canary pool for opt-in customers. I'll follow up with sales/solutions to collect early testers.
DevBot: Canary update at 1769991600: 8/8 instances healthy. Canary prewarm latency improvement observed: avg first-token -62ms.
Jordan: We'll post a short doc with recommended test harness (wrk-like command + sample prompts) tomorrow.
Priya: One last ask — kernel breakages: any mitigation strategy if a new kernel causes p99 regressions?
Samir: Rollback path: autoscaling to safe defaults + automatic fallback to previous kernel binary. We'll open an ops runbook PR with steps.
Lina: Thanks — next steps captured. I'll convert this thread into action items and assign owners. If you want to be an early tester, DM me. :thumbsup:
